description: Text under a glass panel is blurred with the backdrop; text above it stays sharp.

florui.css: .scene { position: relative; width: 220px; height: 120px; background-color: #1b1b2f; overflow: hidden; } .s1 { position: absolute; left: 0px; top: 0px; width: 110px; height: 120px; background-color: #ff5a5f; } .s2 { position: absolute; left: 110px; top: 0px; width: 110px; height: 120px; background-color: #2ec4b6; } .under { position: absolute; left: 20px; top: 20px; font-size: 28px; font-weight: 700; color: #ffffff; } .glass { position: absolute; left: 14px; top: 14px; width: 192px; height: 52px; border-radius: 14px; background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14); backdrop-filter: blur(5px); } .over { position: absolute; left: 24px; top: 78px; font-size: 18px; color: #ffffff; }

classification.reason: Chromium and this engine build a Gaussian blur differently (kernel shape and rounding), so a pixel in the blurred area differs by a few levels of 255 and a pixel at a steep colour edge by more. Measured against desktop Chrome: 4.1% differ by more than 8 levels, almost all of them the glyph edges of the text (Chromium and this engine antialias text differently, as in div-default), 30% by any amount, max 162 on a glyph edge. channel_tolerance 8 stops the harmless rounding from counting; the percentage left is the steep edges. With the backdrop blur read past the panel edge as transparent instead of mirrored (the defect this fixture found), about 30% of the pixels differed by more than that.
